result.summary: Expands shortened IPv6 addresses containing "::" into full eight-group notation before sending them as domain names in SOCKS5 CONNECT requests. This prevents Tor exit relays from misparsing destination "<address>:<port>" strings as an IPv6 address without a port when the port is absorbed as an eighth group. Zone indices and addresses already using all eight groups are left unchanged.
result.problem: Outbound connections through SOCKS5 proxies using Tor fail with "general failure" whenever an IPv6 peer's address contains an inner "::". Tor exits attempt to parse "<name>:<port>" as an address, causing the compressed address to absorb the port number and fail port extraction, dropping roughly 20% of IPv6 peers in addrman and 29% of DNS seed IPv6 answers with no fallback.
evidence: Corroborates with upstream Tor issue #32314 where Tor exit relays misparse compressed IPv6 destinations with appended ports.

Author reports: "About 20% of the IPv6 addresses in a gossip-filled addrman, and 29% of current IPv6 DNS seed answers, have an inner '::'. The failure is closed; there is no fallback to a direct connection."

Mainnet testing against Tor 0.4.9.13: "master could not reach four seed-provided peers with inner-'::' addresses (30 'general failure'); with this change all four connected and completed the version handshake."
result.changed_since_previous: The commit and implementation approach remain unchanged; only minor updates occurred since the previous patch-id.
result.card: Expands compressed IPv6 addresses into full eight-group notation when sending destination hostnames in SOCKS5 CONNECT requests. Outbound connections through Tor SOCKS5 proxies fail with a general failure error for peers whose IPv6 addresses contain an inner double colon, because Tor exit relays mistakenly parse the combined address and port string as an eight-group IPv6 address with no port. The author notes this affects approximately 20% of IPv6 addresses in addrman and 29% of DNS seed IPv6 answers, with no fallback to direct connections. Mainnet testing against Tor 0.4.9.13 confirmed four seed peers that previously failed with 30 connection errors were able to connect and complete handshakes with this fix.

risk.why: A bug in proxy destination address formatting could prevent nodes using SOCKS5 proxies from reaching IPv6 peers.
